chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Ismaʿil ibn Jabir, who said:
I said to Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: “What is the water that nothing renders impure?” He said: “Its depth is two cubits, and its breadth is one cubit and a span.”

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the subject of the ruling on ritual purity
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a cubit, a unit of length
key_terms.ذِرَاعَانِ: two cubits, a measure of depth
key_terms.شِبْرٍ: a span, an additional unit of width
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُهُ: renders it impure or contaminates it with najasah

ai.seo_question: What quantity of water is not rendered impure according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal measure for the quantity of water that is not rendered impure by contact with impurity. It is cited in the context of determining the amount of kurr water in rulings of taharah and najasah.
